name: Senior Cat Checklist
description: A checklist to help owners care for an aging cat with regular vet checks, kidney and dental care, mobility support, and comfort.

items.text: Schedule more frequent senior wellness exams
Ask about bloodwork and urine tests for kidney health
Keep vaccines and parasite prevention up to date
Discuss dental checks and professional cleanings
Track findings and follow-up steps after each visit
items.note: Ask your vet how often your senior cat should be seen

items.text: Watch for increased thirst or urination
Note any drop in appetite or weight loss
Provide easy access to plenty of fresh water
Check for bad breath or trouble eating
Ask about a diet suited to kidney or dental needs
items.note: Discuss any special diet with your vet before starting

items.text: Provide steps or ramps to favorite high spots
Use a litter box with low sides for easy entry
Place food, water, and litter on the main level
Offer soft, warm, accessible bedding
Keep nails trimmed for comfort and footing
Keep a calm, predictable daily routine
Provide warm, quiet resting spots away from drafts
Help with gentle grooming if your cat slows down
Offer easy play and enrichment for the mind
Give plenty of gentle attention and contact
Appetite, thirst, and weight changes
Hiding, vocalizing, or behavior shifts
Stiffness or trouble jumping and climbing
Litter box accidents or straining
Coat, skin, vision, or hearing changes
items.note: Report new or worsening signs to your vet promptly

items.text: Note daily comfort, appetite, and mood
Track good days versus difficult days
Discuss pain management options with your vet
Adapt the home as your cat's needs change
Keep open conversations with your vet about care
This checklist is general information for owners, not veterinary advice; an aging cat's needs depend on its health and individual condition, so always consult a licensed veterinarian
items.note: For any emergency, contact your vet or an emergency animal hospital immediately

faq.q: When is a cat considered a senior?
faq.a: Cats are often viewed as senior in their later years, but the timing varies between individuals. Ask your veterinarian when your cat enters its senior stage and how its care should change.

faq.q: Why are kidney checks important for older cats?
faq.a: Kidney disease is common in aging cats and develops slowly. Routine bloodwork and urine tests can catch it early, when diet and care can help most. Ask your vet which screenings your cat needs.

faq.q: How can I help a senior cat that struggles to jump?
faq.a: Provide steps or ramps to favorite spots, lower-sided litter boxes, and soft, accessible bedding. If your cat is stiff or reluctant to move, talk to your veterinarian about supportive options.

faq.q: Does dental care matter for older cats?
faq.a: Yes. Dental disease is common and can be painful and affect eating and overall health. Regular dental checks and care at home help keep your senior cat comfortable. Ask your vet for guidance.

faq.q: Is this senior cat checklist printable?
faq.a: Yes. Print it or download the PDF, track vet visits and changes, and use it to keep your aging cat comfortable and well cared for.
